heading: About
body: I started on the frontend, took on the backend, and now ship LLM features in production. Ten years in, the stack has changed more than once; what carries over is understanding how the whole system fits together. Most of what I ship is infrastructure other teams build on: low-code platforms, back-office systems, document management, e-commerce. I own architecture and performance on large codebases, and run the code review that keeps them maintainable. React, Next.js and TypeScript on the front, Node.js and PostgreSQL behind it.

language.short: Designed a DSL for a low-code reporting platform, so analysts write formulas themselves instead of filing tickets.
language.detail: Wrote the grammar, the editor and the evaluator: a parser built with Chevrotain and Lezer, wired into a CodeMirror editor with completion and inline errors.

clients.short: Worked directly with clients in the EU and the US: from deciding what to build, through the trade-offs, to what shipped.
clients.detail: Small teams, so the same person owned the frontend, the backend and the release.

platform.short: Owned the frontend architecture of that platform: a widget system configured at runtime.
platform.detail: Every table, chart and text block is defined by the user over data from their own databases, with archive creation and PDF export on top. Built drag-and-resize and undo/redo in-house for performance, and used react-dnd for page ordering and smaller block moves.

payments.short: Built premium subscriptions for a PWA that also runs in native apps: a paywall plus store purchases and restores.
payments.detail: Purchases go through a native bridge to the store, while premium banners and promo-code and referral rewards live in the web app.

ai.short: Took LLM features from prototype to production inside real product flows.
ai.detail: Built retrieval over the product's own documents, streaming responses, tool calling and agent-style flows. All of it runs through OpenRouter rather than one vendor.

performance.short: Kept large tables and charts responsive on codebases too large for one engineer to keep in their head.
performance.detail: Virtualized the big tables, split and lazy-loaded the routes, trimmed the bundle, and cut repeat GraphQL round trips with fragment-level caching.

review.short: Set up the code review process and mentored the developers who joined later.
review.detail: Wrote the specs the code was built from, and the shared rules and prompts the team used with AI coding tools.

personal: Most of my career has been remote, working with German, American, Israeli and Ukrainian teams. The same sentence carries different weight depending on who says it: direct feedback that is normal in one team reads as rudeness in another. Erin Meyer's "The Culture Map" is good on this. Knowing that early keeps you from reading a blunt sentence as a personal problem.
I like difficult problems and play too much Dark Souls. My approach to both is the same: understand how something works before trying harder.
Outside work: manga, long walks and tea. Tea is the only skill on my LinkedIn that was endorsed without me asking.
